- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and price is rising, model often overreacts; cap upward forecast spikes at 5% above recent peak.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% bias upward for first 7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model overcorrects downward; apply 1–3% upward bias to offset lagged correction.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.6), model exhibits mean reversion bias; forecast should be closer to 30-day moving average than to prior day’s close.
- Model tends to overestimate volatility in high-sentiment periods; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% when sentiment >0.7.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply upward bias of 0.5–1.0% per day until trend stabilizes.
